title: Not Our Water (Part 2)
description: The valve never closed, so the river Delphine Street kept is now headed downhill into the Snazzie FM parking lot and toward the studio basement. Ronnie still has all three agencies on the line, none of them owns it, and a fourth department calls in specifically to disown it harder. Barry just wants the valve off.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Welcome back to Snazzie FM. When we left you, Delphine Street had a river nobody would claim. Update for the folks just tuning in. <p:0.3> That river is now in our parking lot, and Barry tells me it is looking for stairs.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It found the stairs, Ronnie. It's going down to the basement. <p:0.3> Is the valve off?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We've still got all three of our guests holding. Patricia, the water has relocated to our building now. Surely at this point it's a little bit yours.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: If anything, Ronnie, it's less ours now. The schematic ends at Delphine. Your parking lot is off the schematic entirely. <p:0.3> Off-schematic water is, by definition, not our water.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [dissatisfaction-hnn] It's the same water, Patricia. It just walked here.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Water that walks somewhere is touring, Barry. We don't own tours.

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: And it's downhill now, Ronnie, which means it's flowing, which means once again, that's not the one we hit. We hit a flat pipe. A pipe with no opinions about hills.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Downhill is gaining momentum, which is kinetic, which is, and I cannot stress this enough, outside my asset class.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It is in OUR basement, Winston!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Your basement is a vault, Barry, and vaults ARE my asset class, so the basement is mine. <p:0.3> The water in it, however, remains firmly not.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: So you'll take the basement but not what's in it.

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: I take it at rest, Ronnie. Bone dry. The moment you add water it changes asset class and ceases to concern me.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Folks, we've actually got a new line ringing in. Caller, you're on Snazzie FM, who's this?

lines.speaker: caller-marcus
lines.text: Yes, hello, Ronnie. Marcus here, Surface Water. <p:0.3> And I want to say up front, before anyone gets the wrong idea, I am calling about the river in your parking lot specifically to confirm it is not ours.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: You called in. To disown it.

lines.speaker: caller-marcus
lines.text: I dialed the second I saw it on the surface, Barry. Surface Water handles lakes, ponds, the river. <p:0.3> A river that arrives by surprise, in a parking lot, with no permit? That's not a Surface Water river. That's a freelancer.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Thank you, Marcus. Finally, a professional.

lines.speaker: caller-marcus
lines.text: And to be clear, Patricia, you're not off the hook just because I'm on it. I'm a different department entirely. <p:0.3> I am here to disown it. Not to explain it.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: [dissatisfaction-hnn] There are now four of you, and the water is winning.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Alright. New plan. We have four agencies on this line. <p:0.3> If each of you owns one fourth of the valve, can the four of you turn it together?

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Can't turn a fourth of a valve we didn't hit, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Decommissioned, all four fourths!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: My fourth is at rest!

lines.speaker: caller-marcus
lines.text: My fourth's a freelancer!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: IS THE VALVE OFF?!

lines.speaker: caller-patricia
lines.text: Not ours!

lines.speaker: caller-winston
lines.text: Not mine!

lines.speaker: caller-darnell
lines.text: Not the one we hit!

lines.speaker: caller-marcus
lines.text: Not a real river!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Ronnie, my chair just floated past the soundboard.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well, by my count, that's four fourths of nobody's water. <p:0.3> Which means, mathematically, the studio is now standing in a perfectly ownerless lake. Congratulations to no one.

lines.speaker: caller-marcus
lines.text: A lake, did you say? <p:0.3> Ronnie, a lake is standing water. Standing water is Surface Water. <p:0.4> ...I'm going to need to call you back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: He hung up, Ronnie.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now that's fair. <p:0.3> So we finally found a department that owns it. He just needs to get here before it's moving again. We'll be right back.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: It's already moving, Ronnie. <p:0.3> It's downstairs filling the basement.
